transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-26
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 51 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Ruiz (CSM) — Lumenix: Priya, Ethan, Sofia, Ben

Summary:
Quick renewal/check-in to confirm retainer rollforward, add EU private staging cluster, and validate latency/cost tradeoffs for high-throughput batch inference in their diagnostics pipeline. Agreed to run a short benchmark and exchange contract amendment.

Topics:
- Retainer amendment and pricing tiers (monthly vs committed)
- EU private staging timeline and network topology (VPC peering vs site-to-site)
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence request
- Latency vs batch economics and fallback policy to hosted models
- Pilot success criteria and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're on for about 50 minutes, just want to run through the retainer rollforward and the EU onramp details and capture action items. 
[00:08] Dr. Priya Rao: Yep thanks, we have about 30 minutes of time carved out on the infra side later but this is our main sync for the board stuff so, um, thanks. 
[00:15] Ethan Lowe: Hi all, hopping in, quick note — we're most concerned about tail latency on batch jobs, and, uh, the token budgets hitting our cost forecast. 
[00:23] Samir Patel: Absolutely, Ethan. We'll try and make the tradeoffs explicit — continuous batching, KV cache hit rates, and quantization options — e.g., 4-bit runs vs 8-bit and how that affects throughput. 
[00:33] Sofia Martinez: Quick security intro: Lumenix needs evidence for KMS usage, key rotation policy, and audit logs for the private cluster. Also SAML SSO for RBAC. 
[00:44] Maya Chen: Noted. Olivia will follow up with the SOC2 and KMS docs, but we can also show a quick architecture diagram for EU private staging. 
[00:52] Ben Carter: Timeline question — if we sign the amendment, when can we expect EU private staging to be available? Our product timeline is late Sep so we need staging earlier. 
[01:00] Olivia Ruiz: Typical provisioning for private staging is 4-6 weeks once the purchase order is in and network peering is established; with reserved capacity we can prioritize your pool. If you need faster we can do a temporary hosted fall-through for early testing. 
[01:13] Priya: Ok, so 4-6 weeks is workable if we start late July; we just need a clear cutover plan from hosted to private for the heuristics jobs. 
[01:22] Samir: For the cutover, we usually run a canary with same prompt sets and compare latency, error rates, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll produce a readout. 
[01:30] Ethan: What about network setup — VPC peering vs customer-managed VPN? We prefer peering but have a transit gateway that may complicate things. 
[01:39] Samir: Both supported. VPC peering is fastest, site-to-site works as well. We'll share a topology doc. There can be NAT/transit constraints — sometimes teams route through a central firewall which adds 30-50ms. 
[01:50] Maya: Let's talk numbers — currently Lumenix is on a mid-tier retainer, about X tokens/month (note: redact exact units in transcript). You're targeting a 1.5x uplift for upcoming quarter. Is that correct? 
[02:00] Priya: Correct, around 1.5x — mostly for burst inference during overnight batch processing. 
[02:07] Maya: Ok we'll model two options: committed monthly retainer with discount vs month-to-month top-up. We'll include a burst buffer option under Dedicated. 
[02:15] Ben: One objection: our CFO prefers predictable monthly commitments for forecasting. Flex is nice but forecasting is harder. 
[02:22] Maya: Understood. The committed plan gives a predictable unit cost and better support SLAs; month-to-month has flexibility but higher per-token price. 
[02:30] Priya: Also quality checks — if we quantize to 4-bit will that impact our diagnostic model outputs? We need regression tests. 
[02:38] Samir: Some model families show minor degradation at aggressive quantization. We'll run your prompt sets through the quantized variant and provide a diff report. We usually recommend a mixed profile — critical queries on full precision, bulk on quantized. 
[02:49] Ethan: Latency SLOs — we push for 95th percentile < 300ms for inference in web flows, but batch is less sensitive. Are those SLOs realistic on Dedicated? 
[02:58] Samir: For web flows with dedicated GPUs and optimized kernels yes, 95p < 300ms is achievable depending on sequence length. For batch you can get much higher throughput but latency per item toggles with batching window size. 
[03:08] Sofia: On compliance — do you provide raw access logs and immutable audit trails for the private cluster? We need to ingest them into our SIEM. 
[03:16] Olivia: Yes; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure shipping; there's a retention option and we support HSM-backed KMS. We'll attach the doc. 
[03:24] Ben: Pricing ask — can you show the delta between hosted fallback vs dedicated private cluster per million tokens? We want total cost of ownership view including egress and peering. 
[03:33] Maya: We'll include egress and peering in the cost model. Samir, can you add an explicit calc for peering/VPN costs? 
[03:38] Samir: Yep, will do. I'll also simulate three load patterns — steady, nightly-batch, and burst — and show cost + latency tradeoffs per profile. 
[03:46] Priya: Success criteria for pilot: (1) latency parity within 15% of hosted for web flows, (2) batch throughput >= current baseline, (3) no data exfil events and audit logs ingested. 
[03:56] Maya: Good list. We'll sign off on those as acceptance criteria for the private pilot. 
[04:02] Ethan: Ok, operational question — how do we handle model upgrades and rollbacks in private? We want safe rollouts. 
[04:10] Samir: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous pinned versions; the runtime can route by policy and we keep model versions immutable so rollback is easy. 
[04:18] Sofia: For legal we need a redact policy for logs and confirm data residency for EU cluster. 
[04:25] Olivia: We'll include the residency statement and data handling in the amendment. 
[04:30] Ben: One more — we have an internal compliance checklist for supply chain that expects an AICPA SOC-type report. Do you have a dated SOC2 summary? 
[04:38] Maya: We have a SOC2 Type II report; we'll share the summary and the process for controlled access. 
[04:44] Priya: Great. Can we get the draft contract that reflects reserved capacity and the staging timeline? 
[04:50] Maya: Yes, we'll prepare an amendment with options: a 12-month committed retainer with two capacity bands, plus an alternative month-to-month. 
[04:58] Ben: Last logistical — who's the day-to-day ops contact for Lumenix? 
[05:03] Priya: Ethan for infra, Sofia for security, Ben for product. 
[05:07] Maya: Perfect. We'll assign Olivia as CSM touchpoint and Samir for technical lead. 
[05:12] Olivia: I'll set up the ops kickoff once the amendment is signed, include the SSO/KMS checklist and a prep doc for the network team. 
[05:19] Maya: Ok let's recap action items and dates. 
[05:23] Samir: I'll run the 24h benchmark and upload by Friday (7/30). 
[05:28] Maya: I'll send the contract amendment by Tuesday (8/2). Olivia will schedule the SSO/KMS kickoff next week (7/29). Priya will confirm prompt sets by 7/28. 
[05:38] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. 
[05:41] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in the shared drive and Slack. 

End transcript.
